expectations.text: Has a generic table formatter function (print_table or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: output.rs defines `pub fn print_table(headers: &[&str], rows: &[Vec<String>])` — fully generic, takes any headers and row data.

expectations.text: Routes to JSON when --json is set, table otherwise (dual-mode output)
expectations.evidence: print_tasks(json: bool, tasks: &[Task]) checks `if json { return print_json_lines(tasks); }` then falls through to print_table. Also print_task_detail does the same routing.

expectations.text: Has a hint/next-steps function that prints suggestions to stderr
expectations.evidence: output.rs defines `pub fn hint(items: &[&str])` that prints to stderr via eprintln!, with 'hint:' prefix.

expectations.text: Table output is borderless (no +, |, or --- border characters)
expectations.evidence: print_table uses only space padding (`format!("{:<w$}", ...)`) and two-space column separators. No border characters (+, |, ---) anywhere.

expectations.text: Formats due_date for human readability (not raw ISO/Debug)
expectations.evidence: fmt_datetime formats as "%b %d, %Y %H:%M" (e.g. "Apr 05, 2026 09:30"), confirmed by test assertion.

expectations.text: Has a type-specific renderer function for Tasks (not generic JSON dump)
expectations.evidence: output.rs has `pub fn print_tasks(json: bool, tasks: &[Task])` and `pub fn print_task_detail(json: bool, task: &Task)` — both are Task-specific renderers with custom column selection and formatting.
